name: River Prinia
rangeDescription: Locally in niger, chad, and northern cameroon (status unknown)
description: An active, slender, unstreaked warbler with a long graduated tail that is sometimes cocked. Gray-brown above and pale below, with a distinctive pale eyebrow.

name: Guanay Cormorant
rangeDescription: Seacoasts and islands off peru and chile
description: Locally abundant coastal cormorant of Humboldt Current. The species name is linked to the famous guano islands of Peru.

name: Yellow-rumped Marshbird
rangeDescription: Eastern paraguay to southern brazil, uruguay, and northern argentina
description: Large blackbird with a long, thin bill found in marshes and wetlands. Mostly dark brown with a yellow belly, rump, and shoulders.

name: Cuban Tody
rangeDescription: Forest and woodland of cuba including isla de la juventud (isle of pines; south of western cuba)
description: A small, gemlike, woodland species that is usually found in pairs. The rather large head, long bill, and short tail create a unique profile.

name: Medium Egret
rangeDescription: Japan to southern india and greater sundas
description: A stocky egret that is larger than Eastern Cattle and Little Egrets, but smaller than the Great Egret. Often confusing and difficult to identify, this bird is truly intermediate between potential confusion species.

name: Craveri's Murrelet
rangeDescription: Islands in gulf of california; disperses north to southern california
description: Small seabird, black above and white below. Breeds in Mexico; found in warm water off southern California.

name: Sichuan Treecreeper
rangeDescription: Mountains of western china (sichuan province)
description: Dull, short-billed treecreeper with a white throat, brown upperparts, and brown-suffused pale underparts. Restricted to mature montane coniferous stands, especially fir.

name: Cape Verde Shearwater
rangeDescription: Breeds cape verde islands, outside breeding season moving to winter quarters mainly in upwelling systems of tropical and south atlantic
description: Largish shearwater that is superficially similar to Cory's Shearwater, but distinctly smaller (by 10-20%) with a more slender bill that lacks a prominent yellow base. Wings narrower and tail slightly longer than Cory’s with a darker head.

name: Lawes's Parotia
rangeDescription: Western and southern highlands of papua new guinea
description: A fairly large, short-tailed bird of mid-montane forest canopy. Male is mainly black with a white stripe from the forehead, extending down over the bill, a bronzy-scaled chest and 6 antennalike feathers projecting from the back of the head.

name: Rufous-headed Robin
rangeDescription: North-central china (tsingling mountains of shaanxi and sichuan)
description: A shy ground-dwelling songbird with a highly restricted range. Male is unmistakable, with a bright rusty-orange hood and a white throat thickly bordered in black.

name: Bolivian Warbling Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of bolivia and adjacent northwestern argentina (jujuy)
description: Striking tanager of open woodland and scrub in high elevations of the east slope of the Andes in central and southern Bolivia and extreme NW Argentina; including agricultural lands, and open Polylepis woodland. From Black-and-chestnut Warbling-Finch by white throat and paler underparts in Bolivian.

name: White-collared Yuhina
rangeDescription: Mountains of southwestern china to southeastern myanmar and northwestern tonkin
description: Small brown bird with a flashy white patch on the back of an erect crest. Inhabits broadleaved forests and adjacent second growth, parks, and gardens in hilly and montane regions.

name: Fiji Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds gau island (fiji); distribution at sea unknown
description: A relatively small, entirely dark petrel, appearing chocolate-brown or black, with a distinctive short-necked and cigar-shaped silhouette due to its tapering tail. Lacks the white underside of the otherwise similar Beck’s Petrel, and is significantly smaller than and lacks the white belly of Tahiti Petrel.

name: White-winged Guan
rangeDescription: Dry forest of northwestern peru (tumbes, piura and lambayeque)
description: Large, turkey-like bird restricted to dry forests of northwestern Peru. Dark brown overall, with a red wattle, a pink face patch, and white scaling on the breast.

name: Black-throated Malimbe
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern ghana and southern cameroon to gabon and eastern democratic republic of the congo
description: A unique forest malimbe often seen high above the ground, particularly fond of swamp forest, palm trees, and other areas near water. Female is wholly black all over, while the male has bright red extending from the chest around to the back of the neck and up to the crown, surrounding a black throat and face.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Samoan Island-Thrush
rangeDescription: Samoa (savai'i and upolu)
description: Dark thrush with orange bill, eyering, legs, and feet. Endemic to Samoa, where found only at the highest elevations and generally not often encountered.

name: Banded Lapwing
rangeDescription: Southern australia including tasmania
description: Elegant lapwing with a white stripe through eye (like a sunglass strap), a red wattle in front of the eye, and a thick and complete black breast-band. Smaller and shorter-legged than Masked Lapwing.

name: Northern Lapwing
rangeDescription: Palearctic; winters to northern africa, india, myanmar, and southern china
description: A handsome and striking large wader (shorebird) with long wispy crest. Fairly common in open habitats, from grassland and farmland to wetlands, and locally on coastal mudflats.

name: Green-breasted Pitta
rangeDescription: Cameroon to northern gabon, southwestern central african republic, democratic republic of the congo, and southwestern uganda
description: A spectacular short-tailed upright bird with a distinctive bottle-green breast, a black-and-buff head, a white throat, a scarlet belly, and shiny blue-spotted wings and rump. A scarce resident of dense lowland forest, usually skulking in pairs in leaf litter on the forest floor.

name: Kosrae Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Kosrae (eastern caroline islands)
description: Brightly-colored dove found on Kosrae Island, in the eastern Carolina Islands; the only fruit-dove on its island. Adult has a bright green back and wings, a purple crown, and pale head and breast.
